newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Huarte agrees capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Huarte agrees capital increase.

text.p: Shareholders in troubled Spanish building firm Huarte gave the go-ahead to reduce the firm's share capital to zero and then increase it to 10.04 billion pesetas in an accordion operation, local media reported on Thursday.
"There is no other alternative because assets have stayed at less than zero," said Huarte chairman Rafael Fernandez.
Huarte suspended payments in mid-March amid allegations by a partner company that it had concealed huge losses.

Following an extraordinary shareholders meeting Fernandez said a partner will take 40 percent of Huarte's share capital next week. This could be Spanish contractors Obrascon, Elsan and Construcciones Sato, reports said.
The company estimates it will take a month for current shareholders to acquire new shares, which will have a face value of 500 pesetas each. Six new shares will be issued for every five old ones.
Shares which are not taken up will be issued for a second subscription period, and then for a third period if necessary.
The capital increase will be carried out after it is confirmed that creditors agree to lift the suspension of payments, at the end of this month.
